uncovered.why: The branch only checks customer type == 'registered'. No criterion explains skipping the check for prior orders. AC-2 (returning customers get no discount) has no code that serves it in this diff.

WELCOME_DISCOUNT_LABEL and WELCOME_DISCOUNT_RATE are covered by AC-1 and AC-3. The spec lists no scope or criterion for app/static/**, so the receipt display change that AC-3 needs is not in this diff.

questions.text: How does the code know a customer has previous orders? The diff reads only customer['type']. What happens for a registered customer who has prior orders, such as returning-customer-01?
Does a guest count as a 'new customer'? The spec leaves this open. The code gives guests no discount.
Is the $50 free-shipping threshold checked against the subtotal before or after the welcome discount? For example, a subtotal of 52.00 drops to 46.80 after the discount.

Which rounding mode applies? The spec says 'nearest cent' but does not say how exact halves are handled. For example, 33.35 x 0.10 = 3.335 could round to 3.34 (half-up) or 3.34 (half-even, since 3.335 goes to the even cent 3.34). Please state the intended mode. to_money is not shown.
Does the discount apply to the subtotal only, or also to shipping, tax or other fees?
What happens with a zero or empty subtotal? Is the label 'Welcome 10%' still returned alongside a 0.00 discount?
Which part of the receipt shows the label? The scope includes app/static/**, but nothing in the diff touches receipt rendering.
Does the welcome discount stack with any other promotion? What happens if a customer places two orders in quick succession, with the first order not yet recorded when the second is quoted?
What happens when the customer dict has no 'type' key, or has an unknown type such as 'admin'? The code would raise a KeyError for a missing key.

proposed_scenarios.why: A registered customer with prior orders must get no discount. The code appears to check only the customer type.
The spec does not define how a guest is treated. This scenario shows the current behaviour so the author can confirm it.
3.335 style half-cent boundary at a tiny amount. 0.05 x 0.10 = 0.005 is an exact half cent.
